summary: Dorzolamide is a topical ophthalmic carbonic anhydrase II inhibitor that lowers intraocular pressure by reducing aqueous humor secretion in the ciliary body. It is used for elevated IOP in open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension. Although given as an eye drop, it is a sulfonamide and is absorbed systemically, so sulfonamide-type hypersensitivity reactions can occur. Common local effects include ocular burning/stinging and a bitter taste.
indications: Elevated intraocular pressure in patients with ocular hypertension
Elevated intraocular pressure in patients with open-angle glaucoma

dosage.n: May be used concomitantly with other topical ocular IOP-lowering agents; if more than one drop product is used, separate by at least 5 minutes
Safety and effectiveness demonstrated in a 3-month pediatric trial; profile comparable to adults

admin: Instill one drop in the affected eye(s) three times daily
Do not let the dropper tip touch the eye or surrounding structures to avoid contamination
If using more than one topical ophthalmic drug, administer at least 5 minutes apart
Remove soft contact lenses before instillation (contains benzalkonium chloride); reinsert 15 minutes after dosing
moa: Carbonic anhydrase catalyzes the reversible hydration of carbon dioxide. Dorzolamide is an inhibitor of human carbonic anhydrase II (CA-II). Inhibition of carbonic anhydrase in the ciliary processes of the eye decreases aqueous humor secretion, presumably by slowing bicarbonate ion formation with a subsequent reduction in sodium and fluid transport, lowering intraocular pressure.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to dorzolamide or any component of the product
relative: Low corneal endothelial cell counts (increased risk of corneal edema)
Severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) - not recommended
monitor: Local ocular allergic and lid reactions

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Dorzolamide caused fetal vertebral malformations in rabbits and growth delays in rat offspring at high oral exposures, but systemic absorption from topical ocular use is minimal. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: There are no human data on the presence of dorzolamide in breast milk or effects on the breastfed infant. Dorzolamide and its N-desethyl metabolite are present in the milk of lactating rats. Weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and potential infant risk.
renal: Dorzolamide and its metabolite are excreted predominantly by the kidney. It has not been studied in patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) and is not recommended in such patients.
hepatic: Dorzolamide has not been studied in patients with hepatic impairment and should be used with caution in this group.

moderate: Oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (potential additive systemic carbonic anhydrase inhibition - concomitant use not recommended)
minor: High-dose salicylate therapy (potential for acid-base and electrolyte disturbances / salicylate toxicity, as seen with oral CA inhibitors)
interactions.diagnostics: Potential for acid-base and electrolyte disturbances (e.g., serum potassium, blood pH) with systemic carbonic anhydrase inhibition

common: Ocular burning, stinging, or discomfort on instillation (~1/3 of patients)
serious: Corneal edema in patients with low endothelial cell counts
rare: Systemic allergic reactions (angioedema, bronchospasm, pruritus, urticaria)

monitoring: Corneal status in patients with low endothelial cell counts
counsel: Instill one drop in the affected eye(s) three times daily as directed
This is a sulfonamide; although given as a drop it is absorbed systemically - report severe skin reactions or signs of hypersensitivity and discontinue
Do not let the dropper tip touch the eye or any surface to prevent contamination and serious eye infection
If using more than one eye drop, wait at least 5 minutes between products
Remove soft contact lenses before use and reinsert 15 minutes later
Seek prompt advice for any ocular reaction, surgery, eye trauma, or infection
pk: IOP-lowering effect follows topical ocular administration
Accumulates in red blood cells via CA-II binding during chronic dosing; plasma levels generally below assay limit (<15 nM)
Slow terminal elimination from RBCs with a half-life of about 4 months after stopping
Three-times-daily dosing maintains IOP control; steady state reached within ~8 weeks
Store at 15-30 C (59-86 F); protect from light
pearls: Although applied topically, dorzolamide is a sulfonamide absorbed systemically - sulfonamide-type adverse reactions (including rare SJS/TEN, blood dyscrasias) can occur
Do not combine with oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors due to additive systemic effects
Caution in patients with low corneal endothelial cell counts because of increased risk of corneal edema
Binds moderately to plasma proteins (~33%) and is excreted largely unchanged in urine
missed: Instill the missed drop as soon as remembered. If it is nearly time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule - do not instill extra drops to make up.
overdose: Systemic overdose may cause electrolyte imbalance, an acidotic state, and possible central nervous system effects. Monitor serum electrolytes (particularly potassium) and blood pH, and provide supportive care.
